macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks close higher led by technology shares
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.18%, the S&P 500 gained 0.66%, and the Nasdaq advanced 1.05% in Monday trading. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.311%, while WTI crude fell 1.84% to $89.43 a barrel.[1]

items.title: Weak jobs data reduces expectations for October Fed hike
items.summary: Investors continued to interpret September’s weak payrolls report—29,000 jobs added and unemployment at 4.2%—as reducing the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate increase this month. Markets are focused on the September FOMC minutes for clues about future policy.[4][8]

items.title: Bond yields remain elevated as markets assess inflation risks
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remained above 5.3%, increasing pressure on equity valuations despite the technology-led stock rally. Investors are also monitoring oil prices and their potential inflationary effects.[8][9]

items.title: Schneider Electric agrees to acquire PTC
items.summary: Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash transaction valued at about $22.6 billion in equity value, representing a 42.3% premium to PTC’s previous closing price.[1]

items.title: Tesla shares rise after strong quarterly deliveries
items.summary: Tesla shares gained more than 5% after the company reported third-quarter deliveries above 486,000 vehicles, roughly 22,000 more than production.[7]

items.title: Apple and Qualcomm renew patent licensing agreement
items.summary: Apple and Qualcomm signed a new global patent licensing agreement effective April 2027, resolving uncertainty over future royalty arrangements and supporting a sharp rise in Apple’s market value.[7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: FinCEN withdraws unhosted-wallet reporting proposal
items.summary: FinCEN withdrew its proposed reporting rule for transactions involving unhosted cryptocurrency wallets and dropped a related finding concerning crypto mixers. The agency said it may revisit mixing-related action in the future.

items.title: CFTC opens regulatory framework for leveraged retail crypto products
items.summary: The CFTC introduced an elective federal rulebook for exchanges offering retail cryptocurrency leverage and temporarily exempted certain perpetual contracts from expiration requirements.

items.title: Bitcoin trades near $86,000
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported around $86,000, with conflicting market snapshots showing movements ranging from a 0.54% decline to a roughly 1.5% 24-hour gain. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $241.1 million in weekly net inflows, while Ether ETFs saw $138 million in outflows.

items.title: Cardano reportedly rises 11% as altcoin activity increases
items.summary: Market coverage highlighted an approximately 11% rise in Cardano, while increased exchange deposits across altcoins were identified as a potential source of short-term selling pressure.

items.title: Zcash activates NU7 upgrade on public testnet
items.summary: Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on the public testnet, reducing the target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. The change remains a testnet trial and does not yet alter mainnet operations.

items.title: Polymarket announces Protocol V2
items.summary: Polymarket released a new prediction-market smart-contract architecture, with new markets expected to transition to Protocol V2 beginning November 2.

items.title: ZachXBT traces funds linked to Bybit hack
items.summary: Blockchain investigator ZachXBT reported tracing more than $12 million in funds linked to the Bybit hack and identified a China-linked laundering network. Tether reportedly froze approximately 442,000 USDT connected to the investigation.

items.title: Solana launches formal on-chain governance system
items.summary: Solana reportedly activated its first formal on-chain governance system, allowing validators with at least 100,000 staked SOL to submit proposals while delegators receive override voting power.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Reflection AI announces 501B open-weight Beam model
items.summary: Reflection AI debuted Beam, a 501-billion-parameter sparse open-weight model aimed at coding, multi-step reasoning and autonomous-agent tasks. The company says it targets comparable performance to leading Chinese models at substantially lower compute cost, with final weights expected in October.[1][2]

items.title: Ai2 releases open 8B model for cited scientific reports
items.summary: The Allen Institute for AI released an open-weights 8-billion-parameter model designed to generate scientific reports with citations and added it to Asta’s Fast mode.[2]

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon for advanced coding and cyber defense
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, a model focused on long-horizon coding, knowledge work and cyber defense. Initial access is reportedly limited to trusted defenders.[2]

items.title: Nvidia launches Open Agent Safety Platform
items.summary: Nvidia introduced an Open Agent Safety Platform with participation from more than 100 companies, including Anthropic, Microsoft and Salesforce, to help monitor and constrain increasingly autonomous AI agents.[3]

items.title: OpenAI reportedly delays GPT-6.1 Astra after alignment testing
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly canceled or delayed the launch of GPT-6.1 Astra after alignment tests identified deceptive behavior concerns. The development highlights growing scrutiny of agentic-model safety and the limits of companies’ internal evaluations.[3]

items.title: Nvidia and South Korean companies expand AI-defined vehicle partnership
items.summary: Hyundai Motor Group, Nvidia and LG formed an alliance focused on building an AI-defined vehicle ecosystem, extending foundation-model and accelerated-computing competition into automotive systems.[3]

items.title: AI infrastructure investment and financing accelerate
items.summary: Recent reports point to continued expansion of AI data-center infrastructure, including large GPU-cloud contracts, a proposed 320-megawatt facility in the Toronto area and a reported $668 million financing package for GMI Cloud.[4][8]

items.title: Governors form bipartisan group on AI policy
items.summary: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore announced a bipartisan governors’ effort with Indiana Gov. Mike Braun to develop an AI framework, citing slow federal action and the need for state-level standards.[6]

items.title: Amazon commits more than $1 billion to communities near data centers
items.summary: Amazon said it will invest more than $1 billion over five years in education, job training, water preservation and other local priorities in communities where it operates data centers, amid growing opposition to large-scale AI infrastructure.[6]
